title: Choose exactly / at most k items
text: Binary x[i] = 1 if item i is chosen. Exactly k: linear constraint sum_i x[i] = k (kind linear, sense eq). At most / at least k: sense le / ge. Put it in constraints, not in the objective; the system builds the penalty. Derive k from the data when it is a confirmed setting.
source: Lucas, Ising formulations of many NP problems, Front. Phys. 2014; Glover, Kochenberger, Du, Quantum Bridge Analytics I, 4OR 2019

title: Assign every item to exactly one option (one-hot rows)
text: Binary x[i,g] = 1 if item i goes to option g (group, team, slot, facility). For every item: sum_g x[i,g] = 1. Options that are not allowed for an item are simply not created as variables (fewer variables, no penalty needed). Decision keys name both sets, e.g. {items: i, groups: g}.
source: Lucas 2014, sec. on graph colouring and partitioning; Glover et al. 2019

title: Balanced groups: every option gets the same number of items
text: With one-hot assignment x[i,g]: for every group g, sum_i x[i,g] = n / G (or le / ge for capacities). Within-group cost (compactness) is quadratic: sum_g sum_{i<j} d[i,j] x[i,g] x[j,g]. Use the data's sizes so a small example stays feasible (n divisible by G).
source: Glover et al. 2019 (clustering / graph partitioning examples)

title: Capacity / budget: weighted sum at most C
text: sum_i w[i] x[i] <= C as a linear constraint with INTEGER coefficients (scale and round weights and C if needed). The system adds the slack encoding; do not add slack variables yourself. For several resources, one constraint per resource.
source: Glover et al. 2019 (knapsack with slack variables)

title: Coverage counted once: indicator per demand point
text: Sites x[s] (open or not) and demand points j with weight w[j]. Use a HELPER indicator z[j] = 'j is covered' with constraint z[j] <= sum_{s covers j} x[s] (linear: z[j] - sum x[s] <= 0) and objective maximize sum_j w[j] z[j]. Then a point covered by two open sites counts once. Summing w over every (site, point) pair instead counts a point several times and makes the objective separable (wrong for 'count each point once'). z gets variable_keys {} because it follows from the decisions.
source: Classic maximum covering location problem (Church and ReVelle 1974) written as a binary model

title: Every demand point must be covered (set cover)
text: For each element j: sum_{sets S containing j} x[S] >= 1 (linear, ge). Minimise the number or cost of chosen sets. For partial coverage with a target use the coverage indicator pattern instead.

title: Nearest open facility: assignment variables (p-median)
text: Open x[s]; assignment y[j,s] = 1 if demand j is served by site s. Constraints: sum_s y[j,s] = 1 for every j; y[j,s] <= x[s] (implication pairs (y, x)); sum_s x[s] = p. Objective minimise sum w[j] d[j,s] y[j,s]. Restrict y to the few nearest sites of each j to keep the size manageable. Only x is the decision (variable_keys {sites: s}); y follows from x, so its variable_keys are {}.
source: Hakimi 1964 p-median, standard integer programming form

title: Routing / closed tour (TSP, inspection or delivery round: visit every stop once and return): position encoding x[i,t]
text: x[i,t] = 1 if stop i is visited at position t (t = 0..n-1). Each stop once: sum_t x[i,t] = 1; each position one stop: sum_i x[i,t] = 1. Distance: sum_t sum_{i != j} d[i,j] x[i,t] x[j,t+1], with t+1 taken modulo n for a closed tour. These two one-hot families already make every feasible solution a single tour: NO subtour (MTZ) constraints or extra order variables are needed. Size n^2. Declare the visit positions as a second set in DATA_SCHEMA (e.g. 'positions', one entry per stop, built in the data step from the stop list) and key each x[i,t] with both sets, e.g. {'stops': i, 'positions': t}; a key name that is not a declared set fails validation.

title: Itinerary: choose m of n stops and put them in order (position encoding)
text: x[i,t] with t = 0..m-1 positions: each position exactly one stop (sum_i x[i,t] = 1); each stop at most once (sum_t x[i,t] <= 1). Distance terms between consecutive positions as in the position tour. Category requirements: for each category c, sum over stops in c and all t of x[i,t] >= 1.
source: Position-encoding variant of the prize-collecting / orienteering problem (Lucas 2014 style)

title: Linking decisions: y may be 1 only if x is 1
text: Use a constraint of kind implication with pairs [y, x] (y = 1 implies x = 1), equivalent to y <= x. For 'not both' use kind exclusion with pairs [a, b]. These are cheaper than general linear constraints.
source: Glover et al. 2019 (quadratic penalties for x <= y and x + y <= 1)

title: Shift scheduling: coverage, one shift a day, forbidden sequences
text: x[p,d,s] = 1 if person p works shift s on day d. Coverage: sum_p x[p,d,s] >= req[d][s]. At most one shift a day: sum_s x[p,d,s] <= 1. Weekly limit: sum_{d,s} x[p,d,s] <= L. Forbidden sequence (e.g. night then early next day): exclusion pairs (x[p,d,night], x[p,d+1,early]). Preferences go into the objective with their weights.
source: Nurse rostering QUBO formulations, e.g. Ikeda, Nakamura, Humble, Sci. Rep. 2019

title: Jobs with start times and precedence (time-indexed)
text: x[j,t] = 1 if job j starts at time t; each job starts once: sum_t x[j,t] = 1. Machine capacity: for each time, jobs running at that time <= capacity. Precedence j before k: exclusion pairs (x[j,t], x[k,t']) for every t' < t + duration[j]. Objective e.g. sum_t (t + duration) x[last,t].
source: Venturelli, Marchand, Rojo, Job shop scheduling solver based on quantum annealing, 2016

title: Integer quantities (how many) from binary digits
text: If the decision is a quantity q in 0..Q, write q = sum_b 2^b x[b] (b = 0..floor(log2 Q)) with an extra constraint q <= Q when Q is not 2^k - 1. Every term with q becomes a sum over its bits. Name the bits clearly; variable_keys of the bits name the item and the bit, e.g. {stations: s, bits: b}.
source: Glover et al. 2019; Lucas 2014 sec. 2.4 (log encoding)

title: Portfolio selection: return minus risk with a cardinality budget
text: x[i] = 1 if asset i is held (equal weights). Maximise sum_i mu[i] x[i] - lambda * sum_{i,j} Sigma[i,j] x[i] x[j] (diagonal terms go to linear, x*x = x), with sum_i x[i] = k. mu and Sigma come from historical returns of the SAME period; lambda is a confirmed setting.
source: Markowitz mean-variance as binary QUBO, e.g. Mugel et al., Phys. Rev. Research 2022

title: Feature selection: relevance minus redundancy
text: x[f] = 1 if feature f is kept. Maximise sum_f r[f] x[f] - alpha * sum_{f<g} R[f,g] x[f] x[g], where r is relevance to the target (e.g. |correlation|) and R redundancy between features; sum_f x[f] = k. Exclude the target and identifier columns from the candidates.
source: Mucke, Heese, Muller, Wolter, Piatkowski, Feature selection on quantum computers, Quantum Mach. Intell. 2023

title: Graph partition / max-cut and community structure
text: x[v] = side of node v. Edge (u,v) cut when x[u] != x[v]: cut = x[u] + x[v] - 2 x[u] x[v]. Max-cut maximises the cut weight (no constraints); balanced bisection adds sum_v x[v] = n/2 and minimises the cut. For more than two parts use one-hot x[v,g].

title: Network design: decide which links to BUILD between nodes (not for visiting stops in an order)
text: y[e] = 1 if edge e is built, x[v] = 1 if node v is served. An edge may be built only between served nodes: implication pairs (y[e], x[u]) and (y[e], x[v]). Each served node needs at least one built edge: sum_{e at v} y[e] >= x[v] (linear: sum y - x >= 0). Budget: sum cost[e] y[e] <= B. Full connectivity is hard to express exactly; state the simplification in MODEL_CHOICE.
source: Glover et al. 2019; Lucas 2014 sec. 8 (tree constraints)

title: Check: does each quantity in the objective count once?
text: When the objective sums a value over pairs (site, point), (team, member) or (asset, period), ask whether the specification counts a point, member or period once. If yes, introduce an indicator per counted thing (see coverage-once) instead of summing over all pairs. A purely linear objective with only a 'choose k' constraint is solvable by sorting: usually a sign that an interaction was lost.
source: Modelling guideline derived from the maximum covering location problem
